title: Zero-differential free graded modules are coproducts of single complexes
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $K^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $A$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with all differentials zero. Let $B_n$ be a set for each integer $n$, and suppose specified $A$-linear isomorphisms $e_n:K^n\simeq A^{(B_n)}$ are given. Then $K^\bullet$ is isomorphic, in the category of cochain complexes, to the coproduct indexed by pairs $(n,b)$ with $b\in B_n$ of the single complex consisting of $A$ in degree $n$. Empty basis sets and the zero ring are allowed.

source.place: Tag 09KN, proof: the upper and lower free graded modules are direct sums of shifts of A

proof.text: For each pair (n,b), define an inclusion from the single complex A in degree n to K. In that degree, send a to e_n inverse applied to the finitely supported vector with coefficient a at b. In other degrees the source is zero. These maps commute with differentials because all differentials of K are zero. The fully proved helper freeBasisIn constructs these maps, and freeBasisCofan collects them into a cocone.

Evaluate this cocone at a fixed degree m. To descend a cocone with target T, send x in K^m to the finite linear combination, with coefficients e_m(x), of the images of 1 under the legs indexed by (m,b). For a leg indexed by (n,b) with n != m, its source is zero, so the factorization equation holds uniquely. For n=m, cancellation of the single-term self isomorphism and the single-vector formula for linear combinations prove factorization. Any other descent agrees on every basis vector by the same factorization equations; Finsupp.lhom_ext proves equality on the free module and the inverse identity for e_m proves equality on K^m. These arguments are implemented without sorry in freeBasisEvalIsColimit.

Apply Mathlib HomologicalComplex.isColimitOfEval to the degreewise colimit witnesses. Hence the explicit basis cocone is a colimit cocone of complexes. Its cocone point is K; compare it with the chosen categorical coproduct using IsColimit.coconePointUniqueUpToIso. This gives the claimed isomorphism. No nontriviality, nonempty basis, finite basis, or degree bound is used.

A cochain complex with zero differentials and free modules in all degrees is a coproduct of single complexes of the ring indexed by a basis in every degree

theorem nonempty_iso_coproduct_single_of_zero_d
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (B : ℤ → Type u) (e : ∀ n : ℤ, K.X n ≃ₗ[A] (B n →₀ A))
    (hd : ∀ i j : ℤ, K.d i j = 0) :
    Nonempty (K ≅ ∐ (fun i : Σ n : ℤ, B n ↦
      (HomologicalComplex.single (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) i.1).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A A)))
